issue.title: Race condition in high traffic sites on Cloudflare Workers with remote JWKS

repository.name: jose
repository.description: JWA, JWS, JWE, JWT, JWK, JWKS for Node.js, Browser, Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, and other Web-interoperable runtimes

issue.body:
### What happened?

On Cloudflare Workers it is not possible for one request to await an unsettled promise that was created by another request because that inverts the control flow and the runtime can't keep track of which task are associated with which request.

The `reload` function at: https://github.com/panva/jose/blob/bd7bf3789c146d765bbee2db0c93ba035020b24c/src/jwks/remote.ts#L91-L111
uses a shared promise `this._pendingFetch`.

So if a second request comes in at the same isolate as another request is updating, this will lead to an exception in the second request as soon as it awaits the unsettled promise.

A work-around is instead of awaiting the promise, to do a setInterval that checks say every 5ms if a condition is changed.

I saw you already have a detection for Cloudflare Workers in `/src/runtime/browser/env.ts` https://github.com/panva/jose/blob/bd7bf3789c146d765bbee2db0c93ba035020b24c/src/runtime/browser/env.ts

My proposed solution would be to create a function `pollingAwait` that wraps the setInterval solution in another Promise so that you can await that. And pick to use either a straight await or a pollingAwait depending on the value in the browser/env check.

### Version

4.3.9

### Runtime

Cloudflare Workers

### Runtime Details

latest version/compatability date

### Code to reproduce

```js
console.log('regular use of the JWKS feature')
```

Hey @panva! Happy to talk with you about our plans for Edge Functions (and the Edge Runtime in general).

I'll send you a message 😄

@panva I was wondering how it would feel to be able to address the runtime in both development and production running something like `typeof VercelRuntime !== 'undefined'`. If it doesn't sound ok, what's the way you'd expect it to work?

Since CF Workers [added](https://community.cloudflare.com/t/2022-3-4-workers-runtime-release-notes/362666) navigator.userAgent. I would expect both dev and production runtimes of next.js middlewares to have the same method of detecting the runtime the code is running in.

more on the workers: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/compatibility-dates/#global-navigator

issue.title: [edge] Make runtime addressable in compile time
issue.body:
this commit allows to use EdgeRuntime as a dead code eliminator identifier:

```ts
if (typeof EdgeRuntime !== "undefined") {
  console.log("will be stripped away");
} else {
  console.log("will be kept in the bundle");
}
```

which means we're replacing `EdgeRuntime` with a literal
